revisions.change_explanation: Initial chapter place: the attested island name with an area-level cited identification and a label anchor, since the historical term covers two modern islands.

content.summary: 多禰島, named in the biography as the island the second ship headed for on 天寶十二載十二月六日 (753), in the passage that places 阿兒奈波島 south-west of it.

geometry.notes: Label anchor at Tanegashima (Wikidata Q696228), the northern island of the area the cited reference work describes for 多禰島. It is not an asserted historical coordinate: the cited work describes an area covering Tanegashima and Yakushima, so no single site is placed.

modern_equivalents.note: The cited reference work describes 多禰島 (also 多褹島) as covering the present-day Tanegashima and Yakushima area; recorded as a scholarly identification.

content.editorial_notes: The identification is area-level, so the geometry stays a display anchor rather than an approximate point; the reader sees where the islands are without an asserted site.

claims.statement: The biography names 多禰島 as the island the second ship set out for on 天寶十二載十二月六日.

locator.value: 十二月六日南風起，第一舟着石不動，第二舟發向多禰去

claims.statement: The cited reference work describes 多禰島 as an island of 西海道 covering the present-day Tanegashima and Yakushima area; the label anchor is placed at Tanegashima's modern coordinate from Wikidata (CC0) and asserts no site.
claims.attributed_to: 山川出版社「山川 日本史小辞典 改訂新版」「多禰島」
